title: Dropbox sold the idea before the product. Its first big test was a three minute demo video.
description:
Its first big test was a three minute demo video. Working software could not yet be shown as a prototype.

on the beta waiting list after the video, up from 5,000

The team hid about a dozen Easter eggs for the Digg audience. The video passed 10,000 Diggs within 24 hours.

Posted his Y Combinator application to Hacker News on 4 April.

He proved people wanted it before he finished building it.

Sources:
- https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=8863 (read): established that Drew Houston posted "My YC app: Dropbox - Throw away your USB drive" to Hacker News on 4 April 2007, and replied in the thread that the business plan was freemium.
- https://techcrunch.com/2011/10/19/dropbox-minimal-viable-product/ (read, published 19 October 2011): established that the video was a three minute demonstration, that Houston said the beta waiting list "went from 5,000 people to 75,000 people literally overnight", that the team "put in about a dozen Easter eggs that were tailored for the Digg audience", that the video passed 10,000 Diggs within 24 hours, and that a working prototype could not yet be demonstrated.
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dropbox (read): established that Evenflow, Inc. was founded in May 2007 and renamed Dropbox, Inc. in October 2009.
